decisions.what: Implementation runs in a linked worktree (.claude/worktrees/surfaces, branch worktree-surfaces) with its own node_modules, per explicit owner directive for this build.
decisions.why: The /goal directive says 'implement in a PR (use a worktree)'. The earlier no-worktree decision (PROGRESS.pipeline.json) was about sharing live Playground state; unit-level work needs only the worktree's own installs, and live acceptance is deferred to the main checkout as before.

decisions.what: metadata.surfaceIntent is a plain STRING — the dictionary asset id. Mechanism is derived from the block name (core/group -> group_background, core/cover -> cover); application knobs (position, size, intensity) ride the dictionary entry and the manifest, never the marker.
decisions.why: One asset, many targets: the marker only has to NAME the asset. Anything richer on the node would be per-application state, which the spec rules out (the dictionary is the cardinality).

decisions.what: Surface markers are minted DETERMINISTICALLY at S8, per section fragment, from the brief's attach list — the model never writes surfaceIntent. Skin+edge nests ONE wrapper group per extra layer (outermost skin first); a dead/baseline section is never skinned.
decisions.why: Exactly the placeholder-pixel and nav-link-injection precedent: mechanical attribute writes into model-authored trees, re-gated by validate + compile. Prompt-hoping the model into emitting markers would make the sequencing rule unenforceable.

decisions.what: The canvas asset is born at S3, immediately after wp_tokens_apply moves the epoch — not in S8 with the rest of the pass.
decisions.why: The spec requires canvas-band ink menus computed from the asset's MEASURED luminance range, and S4 (where menus constrain the model) runs before S8. Born with the tokens, the range exists before any tree; S8 only uploads and ships styles.background.

decisions.what: Under --no-images no surface markers are minted at all (not markers-without-assets).
decisions.why: The published page must be byte-identical to today's flat output — the spec's own acceptance. Inert markers would still change the compiled markup.

decisions.what: The spec's two spot rules ('a spot attached to a skinned band is a violation' vs 'decor on a skinned band requires the spot class (true alpha)') are reconciled via an explicit ground_baked flag on spot entries: only a ground_baked spot on a skinned band is the violation; a true-alpha spot is legal anywhere.
decisions.why: coexistence_rules is the more specific text and names the mechanism (true alpha); reading the cross-check as banning ALL spots on skinned bands would contradict it. The flag makes the distinction mechanical.

decisions.what: Flatness rule quantization: if EITHER chosen style's texture cue starts with 'none', the dictionary must be empty.
decisions.why: The spec names one example from each roster (Bauhaus artistic, Flat Design ui). When one half of the combo IS flatness, texture would betray that half; the model can argue past it only by choosing a different combo.

decisions.what: loud_band routing: a field/pattern surface at intensity 'loud' targets a core/cover (veil = author-set overlayColor + dimRatio); with no cover in the section it degrades to a group skin (recorded), and to the flat band when the instance also lacks group background support. Covers need no support probe.
decisions.why: The inventory gives loud surfaces the cover mechanism but the brief has no cover vocabulary; intensity is the deterministic signal. The degrade chain keeps every failure landing on the reservation.

decisions.what: Patterns ship PNG, not JPEG, after mirror-tiling; spots ship PNG for alpha; field/frieze/canvas recompress JPEG (0.80/0.85/0.80). Chroma-key is a hard threshold (RGB distance <= 48), no feathering.
decisions.why: The seam guarantee is byte-exact only in a lossless format — JPEG artifacts across the mirror seam would smear 'seams impossible by construction'. No feathering keeps identical-input -> identical-output trivially true.

decisions.what: Image replay/capture lane: X_AGENT_IMAGE_FIXTURES replays content-addressed fixtures (sha256(prompt|aspect)) instead of calling Gemini; X_AGENT_IMAGE_FIXTURES_CAPTURE mints them on a real run. Env-only, no config key.
decisions.why: M7 demands byte-identical fake runs including surfaces, and no image replay existed anywhere (the fake provider only replays LLM text). Env-only keeps the config surface unchanged and the lane impossible to leave on by accident.

decisions.what: Each surface asset is uploaded ONCE and its media_id/media_url recorded back into the manifest; later applies (other pages, the canvas ship) reuse the attachment. Surface uploads carry NO alt text. Resume replay: generate skips any asset/slot whose manifest entry still has its file on disk, and S8 spends nothing for replayed births.
decisions.why: A site owns a handful of surface assets applied many times — one attachment per asset is what an admin should find in the media library. Alt on a decorative background is a lie. The replay makes a resumed run re-enter at apply instead of re-buying, which the spec asserts and the old code never had.

decisions.what: The pixel oracle hides the element's ink (color: transparent, textShadow: none) for the clip capture, samples every 4th pixel of the box, and rates the declared ink against the WORST CASE of the measured luminance range; findings keep the flat-lane shape with background = 'sampled(min..max)' plus sampled/ground_min/ground_max fields.
decisions.why: Sampling the glyphs as ground would rate ink against itself (~1:1 always-fail); hiding ink first reads the material alone. Worst-case is the only honest rating over a textured range. Keeping the finding shape means screenTextContrast and the 3/4.5 thresholds needed no fork.

decisions.what: The theme.json preview emitter (x-agent/templates/theme-json/emitter.ts) stays settings-only; styles.background is not mirrored into the local preview or the theme_tokens diff.
decisions.why: Its own docblock: it emits exactly what it can vouch for. The background lands in global styles (verified by the companion's response and, live, via manifest.global_styles), not in settings; a preview claim would be a claim about server behavior this side cannot honour.

deviations.spec_ref: determinism.resume ('Unchanged: a resumed run replays generated assets from runs/<ts>/images/ and re-enters at apply')
deviations.what: That behavior did not exist to preserve — the old pass re-ran S8 whole, re-bought every image, and usually tripped budget_exceeded on resume. It was BUILT here (manifest-based replay + spend-skip) rather than inherited.
deviations.why: The spec describes the intended contract as already true; field-mapping showed it was not. Recording the gap instead of silently claiming 'unchanged'.

deviations.what: Clauses needing a live Playground plus real provider spend (real save() recompile, real-model dictionary authorship, the manual Styles-UI undo, the Victorian/Flat end-to-end runs) are staged in pipeline/tests/accept/surfaces-m7.sh, not executed from this worktree.
deviations.why: Repo precedent (PROGRESS.pipeline.json M7 entry) and the standing owner instruction that the persistent dev instance is never repurposed; the accept script boots its own slot and is a one-command run from the main checkout.
